issue_context.title: Erroneous `IOException` in `TarWriter.WriteEntry` on MacOS
issue_context.body:
### Description

dotnet/sdk-container-builds#246

The new `dotnet publish` container support crashes on MacOS. This appears due to an error in `TarWriter.WriteEntry`.

Specifically, [the stack trace points to this line](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/0ca364767715fee7bc9d0273eec4f30a3c6cc8f0/src/libraries/System.Formats.Tar/src/System/Formats/Tar/TarWriter.Unix.cs#LL85C5-L85C5), but the behavior any deeper than that is pretty opaque to me.

I've written a simple `dotnet new console` app that repros the behavior; here is the stack trace output from running it:

```
Unhandled exception. System.IO.IOException: No such file or directory
   at Interop.Sys.GetGroupName(UInt32 gid)
   at System.Formats.Tar.TarWriter.ConstructEntryForWriting(String fullPath, String entryName, FileOptions fileOptions)
   at System.Formats.Tar.TarWriter.WriteEntry(String fileName, String entryName)
   at Program.<Main>$(String[] args) in /Users/jcarpenter/projects/personal/tar-bug/Program.cs:line 18
```


### Reproduction Steps

On a Mac, in a new empty directory:

1. `dotnet new`
2. Create a file named `example-file.txt`:

```
echo 'Plain text file to be included in a tar.' > example-file.txt
```

4. Replace `Program.cs` with:

```csharp
using System.Formats.Tar;
using System.IO.Compression;

File.Delete("example-output.tar");
using var writeStream = File.Create("example-output.tar");

// Initialization roughly corresponds to crashing scenario in Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers/Layers.cs:
// https://github.com/dotnet/sdk-container-builds/blob/86ad14026fc68bb8967e662f49ffb3c105050bca/Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers/Layer.cs#L47
using var compressionStream = new GZipStream(writeStream, CompressionMode.Compress, leaveOpen: true);
using var tarWriter = new TarWriter(compressionStream, TarEntryFormat.Gnu, leaveOpen: true);

// On MacOS, we're able to write to the tar by explicitly creating a GnuTarEntry instance
var workingEntry = new GnuTarEntry(TarEntryType.RegularFile, "working/example-file.txt");
workingEntry.DataStream = File.OpenRead("example-file.txt");
tarWriter.WriteEntry(workingEntry); // works!

// On MacOS, this crashes with an erroneous System.IO.IOException: No such file or directory
tarWriter.WriteEntry("example-file.txt", "broken/example-file.txt"); // crashes

```

5. `dotnet run`

### Expected behavior

A tar should be created with entries for `working/example-file.txt` and `broken/example-file.text`.

### Actual behavior

Instead, the program crashes when calling [the `WriteEntry` overload that takes two strings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/DOTNET/api/system.formats.tar.tarwriter.writeentry?view=net-7.0#system-formats-tar-tarwriter-writeentry(system-string-system-string)) (line 18 in the minimal repro).

If you comment out the offending line, the program produces a tar successfully.

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

One workaround (that I haven't confirmed myself, but assume _must_ work) is to run this on Windows instead.

Another workaround is to avoid the crashing overload of `WriteEntry` and instead always explicitly create `TarEntry` instances. However, there is a lot of convenience baked into the crashing overload; so this workaround represents a higher implementation burden for creating the various types of TarEntries appropriately.

### Configuration

```
» dotnet --info
.NET SDK:
 Version:   7.0.101
 Commit:    bb24aafa11

Runtime Environment:
 OS Name:     Mac OS X
 OS Version:  13.1
 OS Platform: Darwin
 RID:         osx.13-x64
 Base Path:   /usr/local/share/dotnet/sdk/7.0.101/

Host:
  Version:      7.0.1
  Architecture: x64
  Commit:       97203d38ba

[installed, etc. truncated]
```

### Other information

_No response_
comments:
From the discussion in https://github.com/dotnet/sdk-container-builds/issues/246, the entry should be created even if the P/Invoke fails to retrieve the groupname using the provided groupid. Currently we are throwing an exception in such case, preventing the process to finish creating the tar.

I'll work on a fix soon.

review_comments:
Shouldn't it be "gets"?:

> "When this method returns true, [_this method_] gets the value..."

> the groupName field should simply be an empty string.

Is this what other tar tools do? I wonder if one of them chooses to write the groupName regardless of being non-existent.

> Is this what other tar tools do?

Yes. Here's an example:

```
~/tartest $ touch file.txt

~/tartest $ ls -l file.txt
-rw-r--r-- 1 carlos carlos     0 Jan 24 10:50 file.txt

~/tartest $ sudo groupadd deleteme

~/tartest $ getent group deleteme
deleteme:x:3581:

~/tartest $ sudo chgrp deleteme file.txt

~/tartest $ ls -l file.txt
-rw-r--r-- 1 carlos deleteme     0 Jan 24 10:50 file.txt

~/tartest $ sudo groupdel deleteme

~/tartest $ ls -l file.txt
-rw-r--r-- 1 carlos   3581     0 Jan 24 10:50 file.txt

~/tartest $ tar cvf group.tar file.txt
file.txt
```

Then when inspecting the archive, you can see the gname field (yellow) is empty:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1175054/214384732-de24345c-8ed9-4e63-b3a0-8cafd38cdd66.png)

> I wonder if one of them chooses to write the groupName regardless of being non-existent.

But if the groupname is not known, we cannot write one, and we shouldn't be writing anything else, or we would be tampering with the original data we are archiving.

We only know the gid (it's in its own field in the header). We tried but failed to retrieve the groupname associated to that gid, because it does not exist in the current system, so we can just leave it empty.

Thanks for checking. Does that apply for the other POSIX formats we support? 
`tar cvf --format=ustar group.tar file.txt`
`tar cvf --format=gnu group.tar file.txt`

For the case where you manually build a PosixTarEntry and set [GroupName](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.formats.tar.posixtarentry.groupname), do we write the value even if it doesn't exist?

> Does that apply for the other POSIX formats we support?

Yes. Confirmed, exact same behavior with gnu and ustar: The groupname field is left empty.



> For the case where you manually build a PosixTarEntry and set GroupName, do we write the value even if it doesn't exist?

That case is not affected by this bug because whatever value you set to that property is the value that ends up written in the archive. It does not get validated against the groups available in the current OS.

this is using the pattern that is prone to a famous deadlock
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.process.standardoutput?view=net-7.0#remarks

it will only occur if there is a sufficiently large amount of output, so this could well be fine here, but just FYI that this is not a good pattern to use in general.
